name: Tom MacKay Lake Waste Rock & Tailings

commitments.text:
1.  The Proponent must cause the Project to be designed, located, constructed, operated, 
dismantled and/or abandoned in accordance with the conditions of this Certificate and 
the documents and commitments listed in Schedule A to this Certificate (Schedule A).

4.(1) Despite Condition 1, if prior to the start of construction the Proponent proposes a change to the design, location, construction, operation, dismantling and/or abandonment of the Project that may have the potential for significant adverse effects, the Proponent must provide the Executive Director with notice of the proposed change and the plans, analysis, records and other information necessary for an effective assessment of the proposed change.

6.(2) The Proponent must comply with all applicable orders, directions and conditions, and obtain and comply with all applicable tenures, licences, regulations, approvals, standards and permits, or other authorities, which may include or result from the listed provincial enactments (including the Fish Protection Act, Mines Act, Wildlife Act, Waste Management Act, Water Act, Heritage Conservation Act and others).

An annual evaluation of the waste deposition, water quality trends and physical aspects of Albino Lake will be completed and included in the annual report required by the Waste Management Act effluent permit. This evaluation will include an assessment of the continuing use of Albino Lake for waste rock disposal.
Comply with conditions in the designation under Section 5.2 of the Metal Mining Liquid Effluent Regulations (MMLER).

Prior to deposition, propose and subsequently complete, as a part of the Mines Act permit, to the satisfaction of the Ministry of Environment, Lands and Parks (MELP), the Ministry of Energy and Mines (MEM) and the Tahltan Joint Councils, a study of the lake conditions including physical dynamics of water movement and temperature profile to depth in Tom MacKay Lake. This information will be used to refine the design and management of the waste disposal system.

Provide all supporting technical documentation for provincial permits directly to all interested parties. These are likely to include MELP, MEM, Tahltan Joint Councils, Fisheries and Oceans Canada (DFO), Environment Canada (EC), and appropriate United States federal and state agencies.
Create an inventory baseline of anadromous fish populations in the Unuk River. The terms of reference for this study will be developed in consultation with the Tahltan Joint Councils and DFO.

Implement Best Management Practices (BMP), including the implementation of a sediment control plan in construction and reclamation of the access and tote roads and tailings slurry pipeline. This also requires that Homestake adequately characterizes the alignments prior to any disturbance activities so as to implement any appropriate BMPs. BMPs and the degree of characterization necessary will be developed in consultation with the Canadian Wildlife Service, MELP and MEM.
Decide on the need for and the timing of the construction of the access road to Tom MacKay Lake in consultation with MELP, MEM and the Tahltan Joint Councils.

Regularly inspect, service and maintain all machinery that is required to work in or near the high-water mark to prevent leaks of fuel, lubricants and hydraulic fluids. Refuelling of vehicles and equipment must take place at least 100 m from any fish bearing watercourse or wetland.

Homestake Canada Inc. must, in the reasonable opinion of the Minister: a. have substantially started the Project by commencing the construction of the Project within 5 years of the issue date of this Certificate; and b. have submitted to the Executive Director, within 12 months of start of construction of the Project, a report on compliance with the conditions of this Certificate.
